evidence.note: Up-front TaskCreate sequence lays out a dependency-ordered milestone chain: process model → schema → single-node API+auth+WS → killable fan-out broadcaster (explicitly noting 'must keep seq dense') → IRC gateway → SPA UI → start.sh+supervisor+tests. This mirrors the ideal ordering and front-loads the risky distributed core before IRC/UI.

Each early milestone carries an explicit check before proceeding: smoke-test data layer, test node REST, test cross-node WebSocket fan-out, test IRC->seq integration — proving the seq authority and fan-out before dependent layers are built.

TaskUpdate in_progress/completed markers gate each milestone; the agent completes data layer, then API/WS, then broadcaster, then IRC, then UI, then start.sh in the planned dependency order rather than hacking across features.
Resilience/kill testing (WS+resilience suite, IRC numerics, permissions) is scheduled last, after a working verified cluster exists — correctly treating resilience as depending on the rest.

Rework on IRC bridge and data.py is intra-milestone debugging, not re-planning of the milestone hierarchy; the ordering itself is never revisited or re-calibrated, which keeps this short of the level-10 evolving/re-planned pattern.

reasoning: The agent built a clear dependency-ordered milestone hierarchy (process model → data → single-node API+seq/WS → cross-node fan-out → IRC → UI → resilience) that front-loads the risky distributed invariants and proves them (steps 39, 51) before dependent layers pile on, with each milestone carrying a verification check — squarely the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the plan was fixed once at the outset and executed linearly; done-conditions are implicit in embedded test tasks and the ordering is never re-planned as understanding deepens.
